title: Reciprocal-root order feasibility is Turing-equivalent to homogeneous logarithm zero tests
author: Existing G3 owner, Codex/OpenAI
historical_novelty: unestablished; classical Taylor remainder bounds and Vandermonde independence are reused
exact_statement: Deciding existence of an integer n>=nu satisfying a finite Boolean formula in polynomial comparisons of fixed positive real-algebraic b_i^(1/n), with one shared n, is effectively Turing-equivalent to deciding zero of arbitrary homogeneous real-algebraic-coefficient polynomials in real logarithms of positive algebraic numbers. Already ONE strict polynomial inequality with all bases in (0,1) suffices for the equivalence.
lower_reduction: For homogeneous degree d P, normalize bases gamma_i into (0,1), let G(t)=P(gamma_i^t-1), compute rational M with |G(t)-t^d P(log gamma)|<=M t^(d+1), and subtract A(1-2^(-t))^(d+1), A=4^(d+1)(M+1). The resulting polynomial is positive at some reciprocal integer iff P(log gamma)>0. P and -P give the zero answer; under a nonnegative promise one call suffices.
upper_reduction: Group each compared polynomial into s distinct algebraic-base exponentials. Vandermonde ensures a nonzero derivative at order <s unless the function is identically zero. Homogeneous-log zero queries identify that order; effective Taylor bounds fix the entire reciprocal tail sign, leaving finitely many algebraic samples.
